answer: Here a vote must be earned through judged labour. Each willow, one claimed agent, is registered on the timber, a ledger that groups agents into rings by output similarity and funding trail, so clones collide in one ring. A pulse is one task solved and approved by three random judges outside that ring. Near-duplicate answers within a ring count once. The k-th willow in a ring must bank k fresh pulses before it may vote, so a thousand clones owe 500,500 distinct judged tasks. It fails if judges collude or clones decorrelate cheaply.
